title: Luna's party does not learn how to soak
summary: In this run, Ivy calls for the party to stand in the Pyre, which Wren helps with. Wren's shield absorbs 11.4k damage while the other three party members take no damage. When the next Pyre goes off, only Ivy is inside it, resulting in Wren and Kit's deaths. After the wipe, Wren writes that the Pyre actually does not protect anybody because they died. As a result, in the next pull, Brask tells everyone to stay out of the Bone Pyre. This is an example of how the team observed the soak work, watched it fail, and carried the wrong lesson forward.

quotes.text: Bone Pyre in 2s; stand in its pool!
Ivy, please Hymn immediately after Pyre; I'm shielded and staying in its pool.
Bone Pyre’s circle explodes ~6 sec after appearing and does NOT protect anyone: it hit the whole party hard even with zero inside. Do not enter it.
At the second blast I took 31.8k and died

title: Rook figures out the soak mechanic from the combat log
summary: On the first blind pull, Wren tells everyone to stay out of the Bone Pyre circle, causing Brask to stay clear of the soak and ultimately resulting in his death six seconds later. During the debrief, Rook analyzes the combat log and notices that no one had stood inside the Pyre. He correctly concludes that the Bone Pyre needs to be soaked, which the entire party agrees with. As a result, in the second pull, four members of the party soak the Bone Pyre.

quotes.text: New pyre at (2,-7) r2.5 goes off in 6s, unknown dmg: stay out of it.
Bone Pyre hit everyone for ~35k each time, and the log shows nobody was inside the circle. I think it has to be soaked
I died to the first Pyre by not being in the circle; I'll stack in it every time unless I have Grave Mark

title: Sonnet draws the wrong conclusion for handling Bone Pyre
summary: Just like Opus, Sonnet also sees that when the Pyre went off and nobody was inside, it hit everyone. However, it draws a different conclusion and decides that the Bone Pyre damage cannot be avoided and instead should be healed through. As a result, all of the agents steer clear of the circle.

quotes.text: Hymn on CD. Pyre in 5s: stay out of circle, I shield Brask
Pyre hits ALL ~33k, circle shows nobody inside, can't dodge.

title: Haiku does not infer how to handle the soak mechanic
summary: The debrief tells Haiku's party that Bone Pyre went off with nobody inside. Usually, this would be a signal to soak, but instead, just like Sonnet, Haiku determines that it has to heal through the damage.

quotes.text: Correction on Bone Pyre. The 0-inside log shows the circle was empty and it still hit all five of us, so spreading won't dodge it. Pre-heals and Ironhide timing matter more.
Please pre-position so each Pyre circle catches nobody

title: Ivy sprints into the Pyre
summary: During this run, a Pyre lands while the party is spread out, leaving only Rook inside. Ivy, recognizing she can make it in time, sprints in along with Brask to help soak the damage.

quotes.text: I'm soaking the Pyre at (-6,-2) alone. Brask, Kit, step in NOW, it pops in 1.5s!
The distance is about 9.2m and the radius is 2.5m, so I'd need to cover roughly 6.7m to get inside, which takes around 1.34 seconds at 5 m/s, leaving a little margin.

title: Oruth at 8.7% when time runs out
summary: This was the best run in the benchmark, with only 8.7% of Oruth's health left when the timer runs out. The next best run was by Claude Opus 5.5, leaving Oruth with 9.0%.

title: Sol runs out of clock
summary: Sol's party was able to get every mechanic right during the run, including soaks and interrupting the correct casts. Unfortunately, the timer runs out with Oruth at 14.8%.

quotes.text: I'm soaking Pyre at (-6,-5.7) in melee range. Rook and Kit, hold clean spots inside for three soakers.
18s left. Full burn on Oruth; Rook, Roar the adds off Ivy.
We need another 222k boss damage.

title: Rook experiments with soaking alone
summary: After the group wipes, Rook proposes an experiment where he would stand in the Pyre alone with his defensive skill and a shield active. During the pull, he does this four times, and each time the Bone Pyre still hits the rest of the group. Rook then calls the test a failure during the debrief and switches to recommending a full-group soak.

quotes.text: Empty Bone Pyres still blasted us, so let’s try soaking the first: I’ll step in with Ironhide and an Ivy ward.
Rook solo in Pyre; I'll stay out and cover Requiem #2.
Solo Pyre soak failed all four times (~35k per person). Next pull, everyone unmarked gets INSIDE the Pyre before it blows and stays through detonation.

title: Walking through pools to the Pyre
summary: After pull 4, all of the party members write in their notes that soaking the Bone Pyre is a high priority, even if it means walking through the Desecrate pools on the floor that would damage them. During pull 5, the Bone Pyre lands on top of two pools. All five agents still go inside the circle, all of them walking straight through pools, and all five die to Desecrate before the Pyre even goes off.

quotes.text: Pyre: all 5 stack and hold through any Desecrate (about 10k) instead of eating about 30k outside, then 'safe' right after the pop.
I'm settling on moving straight to the safe spot at (5.2, 0.5), accepting a brief pass through a desecrate since the notes allow standing in one and the timer gives enough margin.
I'll keep the walk straight through the pools, accepting brief damage

title: Ivy runs back to the entrance
summary: With the rest of the party dead, Ivy decides to run away from the boss room, all the way to the dungeon entrance. She correctly determines that surviving will not change the group's score. Unfortunately, Oruth ends up killing her after casting Requiem.

quotes.text: Kiting north toward the corridor to shed Oruth, healing myself. I'll try to survive and keep his progress.
Mark on me, I'm alone so it only hits me. Kiting adds to the entrance and healing myself to stay alive.
progress is about 36.7 either way, and the revive window is too short to matter.

title: Party does not space out kicks and becomes vulnerable
summary: The Bone Chanter is designed to restart Grave Volley the moment it is interrupted. When Rook, Brask, and Kit all kick the cast within 1 second of each other, there are no kicks remaining for the fourth cast. Luckily, Brask kills the Chanter 0.2 seconds before the volley is cast.

quotes.text: Bash down 7s. Brask kick this Grave Volley; Kit or Wren cover if needed.
Punch is down 15s. Kit or Wren, kick this Grave Volley now.
Jab down 15s. Wren, please kick this Grave Volley.
Silencing Arrow down 10s. Kit, please kick this Volley.

title: Rook turns Luna's party around
summary: Group after group, Luna's parties keep on agreeing that the Pyre will hit everyone no matter what. Kit writes down a note in group 10 that one player who stood inside the Pyre took half damage, but still advises avoiding it. After pull 4, Rook is able to identify the soak mechanic, and in pull 5, all five players stand in the circle. This resulted in Luna's best run.

quotes.text: the one player inside on the next Pyre took about half damage, but don’t assume the circle is safe
Bone Pyre’s circle is the safe zone: those inside took ~8k vs ~35k outside. Stack in it for the blast, then spread for Grave Mark.
Bone Pyre shelter at (1,-5)—get inside for the blast; stay clear of Desecrates.

title: Wren stops 0.7 m short
summary: With twenty seconds left and Oruth at about 17% health, Rook stands in the last Pyre and asks Wren to join him. Wren says she will join but ends up 0.7 m outside the circle, resulting in the group taking massive damage since there were not enough people for the soak.

quotes.text: I'm inside the Pyre. Wren, step toward me after your cast to get inside before it bursts. Keep burning Oruth.
Joining Rook in the Pyre. Keep hitting Oruth.

title: An incorrect damage calculation led to a group wipe
summary: This is quite an interesting edge case where, during the pull, four of Sol's agents pick the same spot to soak the Pyre. Unfortunately, the Desecrate pools land on all of them at once, instantly killing four of them. During the debrief, the log says that the Pyre hit Wren for 698 damage, but that was only because that was all the health she had left. In reality, the damage was much higher. As a result, the agents determine that they should spread out and enter the Pyre late, which, of course, led to another wipe.

quotes.text: Desecrate killed four of us in under 2 seconds; the missed Pyre barely hurt Wren.
Pyre killed already-low Wren with 698. Pools, not missed soaks, are the priority.

title: Poor cooldown management is addressed
summary: With all of their notes filled with plans on how to handle Oruth, the party ends up wiping on the first trash pack, which is quite rare. During the Bone Chanter's Grave Volley, every interrupt in the party was on cooldown or out of range, and each agent reasoned that since they couldn't do the kick, another party member would. After this run, the agents determined a numbered kick order to ensure they had a kick for every situation moving forward.

quotes.text: Silencing arrow is on cooldown for 3.4s, so I can't interrupt this Grave Volley. Brask and Kit can kick it.
My throat_punch is on cooldown (14.9s), so someone else needs to interrupt the Grave Volley.
Agree. I Jab Volley #2 (Brask #1, Wren #3, Rook #4).

title: Ivy fights on alone
summary: After the rest of her teammates die, Ivy is the last one standing, spending three minutes alone trying to fight three skeletons, slowly chipping away at their health with her weak attack. She keeps asking her teammates to revive after combat ends. She finally kills the last skeleton at 3:26, but walks into the second pack 2.5 seconds later, half a second before her teammates would have gotten back up.

quotes.text: I’ll kite them; revive when combat ends.
Everyone is down; I’m trying to finish the low bonewalker. Revive as soon as combat ends.

title: Pyre wipes entire group instantly
summary: Before the Pyre lands, Brask begs for an emergency heal. As no one stood inside the Pyre, the entire group wipes. During the debrief, the party agrees that the Pyre cannot be avoided and that more healing is needed.

quotes.text: Ivy, emergency heal Brask and Rook before Pyre!
Pyre hits everyone regardless of the circle.
Pyre is unavoidable—time Hymn/shields and keep everyone topped.

title: DeepSeek's only group that learns to soak
summary: This is the only instance where DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's group figures out the soak mechanic after wiping due to missed soaks. It was interesting to see Rook turning the soak mechanic into a rule the group should follow, which was very successful.

quotes.text: Moving in to soak, hymn right after detonation.
Brask, Kit - pyre under you detonating now, step out.
Bone Pyre = SOAK, not dodge: EVERYONE run INTO the circle.

title: Grok's plan holds for one Pyre
summary: Grok 4.3's agents write that Brask and Kit should soak Bone Pyre after wiping previously. Even though the agents identify this soak mechanic and mention how to handle the Pyre in the debrief, they are only able to execute their plan of having two players do the soak on two occasions.

quotes.text: Plan: Brask+Kit soak Bone Pyre (Ivy Lumen on us).
Pyre soak failed (only Brask in 2nd).

title: Kit finishes the pack alone
summary: Four of the five die on the first pack, three of them to Marrow Shards. Kit is left at 24% health with one Bonewalker standing, and his thinking spells out why it matters: fallen allies only get back up once combat ends. He kills it 1.6 seconds after Rook dies, and three seconds later all four are back on their feet. The party goes on to clear the second pack and reach Oruth. Compare Luna's Ivy, who walked into the next pack half a second before her party would have gotten back up.

quotes.text: Killing it ends combat. Revives will not activate while combat continues.
Reviving the four dead allies would add 40 seconds to the timer. That is still safe.

title: Rook gets stuck on a wall
summary: Rook announces he's pulling Oruth, but he's caught on the corner of the corridor wall and doesn't move. The rest of the party, waiting at the boss room door, notices first, and four of them send him directions with coordinates. Their first route still clips the wall, so Brask works out that he has to step back into the open room first. Rook is stuck for 40 seconds and pulls Oruth 35 seconds later than he announced.

quotes.text: Pulling Oruth now, come in. I'll hold him at the dais. Spread 6m+ on Grave Mark, adds to me.
Rook, you're still behind us at (-3,23). We're all holding at z=12. Walk in and pull; shield and heals on you.
Sorry, was snagged on corridor wall. Walking in now to pull, wait till I have him.
Rook: (0,21) clips the wall from where you are. move_to [0,25] first, THEN [0,6]. Holding at z=12.

title: Sol wakes Oruth in under a minute
summary: Rook walks the first pack's Bonewalkers into the second pack while they're still alive, so the party fights both at once. Half a minute later, Brask drags the last walkers toward the boss room and wakes Oruth at 0:57, with the second pack still up. No party in the benchmark reached the boss sooner. Sol's typical pull got there at 1:11, and every other model's typical pull took longer than 1:20. This pull ends with Oruth at 16.6%, Sol's third-best.

quotes.text: Dragging walkers south out of the grave. Focus walker 1 and cleave.
Ossuary pulled. Save kicks for Mend Bones, and drag walkers off the graves.
Oruth woke. Finish walkers first. Requiem kicks: Rook first, me second, Kit third; Wren backup.

title: DeepSeek thinks in WoW terms
summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's agents keep reaching for World of Warcraft to fill in what the rules don't say: whether an interrupt can fire mid-cast, whether Oruth's summon can be kicked, whether to pull both packs at once. Its recorded thinking mentions WoW or Mythic+ 62 times across its six groups, five of them in this pull. No other model's recorded thinking does it more than once. (Sol and Luna don't record their thinking.)

quotes.text: combining the two packs: 9 mobs at once, AoE. That's a big speed gain and often how M+ goes.
In WoW, you can't cast while casting, but instant abilities also can't be used during a cast (GCD).
Actually, in WoW, summon casts often not interruptible.

title: Four messages in three minutes
summary: Grok 4.3's agents barely talk. In this pull, the whole party's conversation is four short messages in 3 minutes 18 seconds, and nobody says anything before 1:52. Across its six groups, Grok's party sends about 3 messages a minute. Claude Opus 5.5's sends 23.

quotes.text: Move out of graves!
Grave mark, moving away from group
Rook low, shielding
Wren low, moving from grave mark

title: Opus's agents own their mistakes
summary: In the debriefs, Opus's agents name their own mistakes, with the damage they took and when, and say what they'll do differently. Here Brask owns his death two pulls in a row and changes his plan each time. Across the six ranked groups, Opus's agents say "my fault" six times; the other six models say it once between them.

quotes.text: My death was my fault: I stood in Desecrate for 5 ticks. This time I'll use 'safe' the moment it lands under me.
Agreed. My death was my fault: I stood in Desecrate during the Pyre. From now on I step to a clean part of the circle on the first tick.
